The laptop drive shouldn't have any issue being on 24/7. Despite the machine being on, the drive is not always in use, and most operating systems will power down a drive in times of inactivity to save power. The question really is what spindle speed both drives are. If the smaller drive is 5400rpm like I suspect, it could be slower than the desktop drive. That's also assuming the desktop drive is running 7200rpm though. But I think ultimately, you answered your own question at the end there, just use both.

Yeah I was thinking about using them both, but I was a little worried about the laptop drive being on all the time. Everyone keeps telling me "laptop drives are not made for long periods of use, that's why laptops suspend/hibernate, to protect them".

That's not really true... I mean, sure, the drive isn't intended to be written/read CONSTANTLY INDEFINITELY, but even a moderate use house server wouldn't fall under that category. Unless you're planning to use this for a continuous write scenario (e.g. home surveilance), you'll be fine. The drive won't actually be active all the time, and the OS will shut it down. The main concern here is heat of the drive, since the laptop drive is smaller it has less surface area to dissipate heat.
